headline: Britain's spy chiefs have warned the cabinet that AI could become one of the country's biggest national security threats.
score_reason: Pool score 7 lowered by 1: the original is behind a subscription wall, the briefing date is unclear, and nothing here is a new decision or event.
importance_line: Ministers are being told that AI-enabled attacks are a leading national risk, which bears on everyone who relies on government and online services, but the briefing was a regular one and no specific threat is named.
summary: The Sunday Times reports, as relayed by International Business Times Singapore, that the heads of MI5, MI6 and GCHQ (Britain's domestic, foreign and signals-intelligence agencies) told the cabinet that hostile states such as Russia and Iran, terrorist groups and lone actors could exploit AI, in a regular threat briefing that was not prompted by an imminent danger. The relay also reports that government 'hackathons' this summer found 407 security weaknesses across nine government bodies, one rated critical, at a cost of about 13,000 pounds, and that one minister reportedly compared the situation to the early COVID-19 pandemic.
notes: The Times page returned HTTP 200 but no article text (subscription wall), so the text was read on International Business Times Singapore (https://www.ibtimes.sg/uk-spy-chiefs-warn-ai-could-become-one-britains-biggest-national-security-threats-94952), which credits The Sunday Times. The relay gives the briefing date as 8 Sep, which looks doubtful, so no date is printed. Source set to The Sunday Times; the pool lists it as The Times.
